key_insight: The paper uses reduced-order reinforcement learning to learn boundary control for suppressing vibrations in a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest beam, and compares the learned policy against a classical LQR controller.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for active vibration suppression in flexible structures where boundary actuation and actuator limits matter.
method: Model the beam with a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest PDE and simply supported boundary conditions.
Derive a reduced-order model via eigenfunction expansion and truncated Galerkin projection.
Formulate the finite-dimensional control problem as a continuous-time MDP and train a PPO controller; benchmark against LQR.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic numerical comparison between PPO and LQR, focusing on vibration reduction, energy dissipation, and actuator constraints.
watch_item: ROM accuracy and boundary-actuation feasibility may limit performance when the truncated dynamics or actuator constraints are too restrictive.
paper_title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
